results.title: Michael Kaminsky's Post - LinkedIn
results.content: The whole point of media mix modeling is to understand the levers that impact your business so that you can manipulate them, and that means understanding causality – not just correlation. Like isn’t the whole point of doing an MMM to be able to optimize your marketing budget? Based on your experience, can you argue for why most mmm models cannot be fundamentally causal despite our best intentions, and efforts? Sellfore Experiments lets marketers run causal, science-backed experiment analysis in minutes, not months, connecting the dots between spend and real incremental impact. Here’s what you can do with it:  🔬 Run geo lift and conversion lift tests in minutes  📈 Validate and calibrate your MMM with causal evidence  📊 Get a single source of truth for every marketing experiment ✨ Turn data into action with AI-generated summaries This is a monumental step towards making scientifically rigorous measurement simple, scalable, and accessible to every marketer.

results.title: Yuya Sasaki - Professor of Economics - RESEARCH
results.content: Abstract:   We propose methods for estimation and uniform inference for a broad class of causal functions, such as conditional average treatment effects and continuous treatment effects, under multi-way clustering. Abstract:  This paper presents novel methods and theories for estimation and inference about parameters in statistical models using machine learning for nuisance parameter estimation when data are dyadic. Abstract:   We introduce a novel method for estimating and conducting inference about extreme quantile treatment effects (QTEs) in the presence of endogeneity. We propose a novel doubly robust score for double/debiased estimation and inference for the unconditional quantile regression (Firpo, Fortin, and Lemieux, 2009) as a measure of heterogeneous counterfactual marginal effects. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method is less biased than under-fitting fixed effect estimators, is more efficient than over-fitting fixed effect estimators, and robustly allows for inference that is as accurate as the oracle estimator. Abstract:  We propose methods for constructing lower bounds on the standard errors of parameters estimated from moment conditions obtained across different samples.
